hero.title: Lovely Professional University
hero.summary: LPU’s School of Agriculture in Phagwara brings crop, livestock and post-harvest learning into one academic setting. Farms, a dairy unit, protected cultivation and subject laboratories support its broad bachelor’s programme, while master’s routes offer specialisation in production, crop improvement, plant protection, soils and horticultural subjects.

overview.heading: Agriculture foundations and specialist postgraduate study
paragraphs: LPU’s agriculture school brings crop, livestock and post-harvest learning into one academic setting. Its facilities page identifies an animal husbandry and dairy unit, agricultural farms and subject laboratories. The breadth matters when comparing a general agriculture degree with a focused postgraduate specialisation.

The bachelor’s degree offers a broad entry to agriculture, while the school’s master’s subjects allow a closer focus on agronomy, genetics, plant protection, soils or horticulture. These choices share an agricultural setting but serve different stages of study. The official CUET 2026 mapping supplies a dated bachelor’s eligibility reference, and the admissions office can clarify how that route fits the intended intake.

admissions.heading: Applying to LPU
admissions.intro: Use the 2026 CUET mapping for bachelor’s subject requirements and the dated School of Agriculture article for master’s entry combinations. Confirm the governing prospectus, counselling route and fee statement with LPU. The live B.Sc. Agriculture page now advertises Admission 2027. The 2026 CUET mapping and dated 2026 school guidance below retain their historical session; obtain the 2027 rules before a next-cycle application.
eligibility_points: For the 2026 CUET mapping, 60% in 10+2 with English and three listed science/agriculture subjects is required.
The mapping specifies English plus PCM, English plus PCB, or English plus Agriculture as CUET subject combinations.
For master’s entry, the school’s May 2026 article specifies 60% in accepted bachelor’s degrees and LPUNEST merit. Check the specialism’s degree combinations.

scholarships.heading: Scholarships and financial support
scholarships.text: LPU publishes university-wide scholarship categories based on academic performance, LPUNEST and other achievements. Agriculture applicants must establish which category and renewal conditions apply to their exact programme.

schemes.name: LPUNEST-linked scholarship
schemes.details: The official scholarship page identifies performance in LPUNEST as one basis for scholarship consideration; no individual award is promised.

placements.heading: Career support and outcomes
placements.text: The university's NIRF 2026 Agriculture and Allied Sectors submission reports graduates, placements, higher-study progression and the median annual salary of placed graduates for the cohorts below. The figures apply to the reported programme-duration group, rather than an individual specialisation, and do not predict an applicant's future outcome.

faqs.question: Which campus location appears in the ICAR record?
faqs.answer: The accredited unit is the School of Agriculture, Phagwara.

faqs.question: Does this record include agriculture master’s courses?
faqs.answer: Yes. It includes eight named master’s specialisations as well as the bachelor’s degree.

faqs.question: What is the ICAR term for LPU’s listed programmes?
faqs.answer: The audited term is 1 April 2023 to 31 March 2028.

faqs.question: What is the verified 2026 B.Sc. Agriculture eligibility at LPU?
faqs.answer: The NTA CUET UG 2026 mapping requires 60% in 10+2 with English and three subjects from Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture. Confirm the age cutoff, because its age sentence still refers to December 2025.

faqs.question: Does the school show protected cultivation facilities?
faqs.answer: Yes. The official school page lists a Hi-Tech Polyhouse.

faqs.question: Can a scholarship amount be assumed from LPUNEST participation?
faqs.answer: No. LPU’s scholarship page describes several categories; the award depends on the applicable programme rules and performance.

faqs.question: Are verified agriculture placement figures available?
faqs.answer: The NIRF 2026 agriculture/allied submission reports UG four-year programmes (2024-2025): 359 placed from 449 graduates in minimum time, with ₹6,60,000 median annual salary among those placed; PG two-year programmes (2024-2025): 160 placed from 193 graduates in minimum time, with ₹7,20,000 median annual salary among those placed. These are historical group-level outcomes, not specialisation-level placement promises.
